title: Plan cutting, machining and assembly
intro: A production plan connects each part to a drawing revision, operation sequence and inspection point. Learn to release work in controlled stages instead of treating a cutting list as a complete manufacturing instruction.

sections.title: Freeze the production inputs
sections.text: Start with an approved drawing revision, stable part codes, material, thickness, grain direction and exposed edges. Distinguish finished size from any process allowance defined by the production method. If a drawing changes, identify affected parts and withdraw obsolete instructions. A part should point to one controlling revision, not leave conflicting dimensions for the operator to resolve.
sections.caption: Part codes connect drawing, parts list and operation sheet.

sections.title: Order operations by dependency
sections.text: For a teaching cabinet side, identify a datum face, cutting, the system-specific order of edge treatment and holes, then trial assembly. Ask whether the next operation will conceal a measurement surface or block tool access. Some faces may need finishing before assembly. There is no universal sequence; this plan describes outputs and checks, not machine operating procedures.
sections.caption: Concealed references and access affect the operation order.

sections.title: Place a check before repetition
sections.text: Before repeating the operation across a batch, check the first part against the drawing: code, datum, finished dimensions and prepared features. Record the result, reviewer and release decision. If a mismatch appears, isolate potentially affected parts and identify the last verified stage. Forcing parts together does not replace dimensional checking or correction of the cause.
sections.caption: First-part approval precedes batch release.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: A teaching batch contains 12 sides. Inspection of the first finds a hole located from the wrong datum. Hold the batch, correct the reference and instructions, and decide the disposition of that part before producing the remaining 11. A tight schedule does not justify repeating the mismatch.
example.decision: Decision: hold repetition, correct the datum, then recheck the first conforming part.

quiz.question: When should the operation be released across the batch?
options: After first-part inspection and documented acceptance
quiz.explanation: Early verification prevents a reference or dimension error from propagating.

assignment.prompt: Prepare a cabinet-side operation sheet with part code, revision, three dependent stages, inspection point and mismatch response.

faq.question: Does an operation sheet qualify someone to operate a machine?
faq.answer: No. Machine operation requires separate competent training, approved instructions and appropriate supervision.
